metadata.scenario: A customer wants to cancel a scheduled service and asks about the cancellation policy. Category: Cancellation. Flags: cancellation_risk.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret speaking. How can I help you today? Hi Margaret, this is George Williams. I’d like to discuss canceling my next cardiac care monitoring appointment. Hi George, thanks for calling. I’m sorry to hear you want to cancel. Can I ask why? Well, I’m feeling better lately, and I think I might not need the service anymore. That’s great to hear you’re feeling better! Just to clarify, would you like to cancel the upcoming appointment scheduled for next week? Yes, that’s correct. Could you also let me know about the cancellation policy? Of course. Our cancellation policy states that if you cancel with less than 24 hours’ notice, there may be a fee. Otherwise, you can cancel at any time without penalty. Got it. So, I wouldn't be charged since I’m canceling a week in advance? That’s right, you won’t be charged for canceling now. Would you like me to confirm the cancellation in our system? Yes, please do. Okay, I’ll go ahead and process that cancellation for you. Thank you. Also, do you think it's a good idea to keep some follow-up appointments scheduled? Well, it can be beneficial, especially after heart surgery. Regular monitoring can help ensure your recovery continues smoothly. That makes sense. How often should I consider follow-ups? Typically, bi-weekly or monthly appointments are recommended for a while after surgery. Okay, I’ll think about setting those up. What would the cost be? Cardiac care monitoring is priced at $80 to $100 per session, depending on the services required. I see. I’ll consider that. Great! Would you like me to schedule a follow-up appointment for you now? Not right now. I’ll call back once I decide. That sounds good, George. I’ll confirm your cancellation. Is there anything else I can help you with today? No, that’s it. Thanks for your help! You’re welcome! Have a great day, George. You too, bye! Goodbye!
